meta.purpose: Hypothesis registry for evaluating NON-LLM, fully-local, performance-optimized models on Unown's learning-layer subtasks: local ONNX encoders (embeddings + cross-encoder reranking) via transformers.js/onnxruntime-node, and zero-model symbolic lanes (MinHash-LSH dedup, LexRank extractive curation, activation scoring). Companion to benchmarks/local-llm (H1-H8, the small-LLM lane); every hypothesis is falsifiable with explicit metrics, thresholds, guards, and a verdict updated by the testbench (benchmarks/nonllm/runner.mjs).
meta.method: Fixtures captured from the live engine (benchmarks/nonllm/fixtures, merged with the earlier generation in ../local-llm/fixtures for failed-run coverage). Local lanes run in-process via transformers.js (q8 ONNX, CPU); remote baselines (triage labels, relevance/importance judgments, dream outputs, blind judging) go through the llm-bridge. Cross-platform validated by the N0 probe on GitHub Actions (ubuntu/macos/windows) and locally under BOTH Bun and Node.
meta.remoteBaseline: kimi-k2.5 via llm-bridge -> Dashscope (list $0.49/M in, $2.50/M out)
meta.localEngine: transformers.js 4.3.1 (Apache-2.0) + onnxruntime-node 1.30 (MIT) — prebuilds for linux-x64/arm64, darwin-arm64, win32-x64/arm64; darwin-x64 prebuilds absent since ORT 1.23 (onnxruntime#27961 — wasm fallback lane required there); Bun supported since Bun 1.2.6 fixed bun#18079

localCandidates.bge-small: Xenova/bge-small-en-v1.5 q8 (~35MB, 33M, MIT, MTEB 62.11) — embedding lane
localCandidates.minilm: Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 q8 (~23MB, 22M, Apache-2.0, MTEB 56.26) — embedding comparison lane
localCandidates.rerank: Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 q8 (~23MB, 23M, Apache-2.0, nDCG@10 ~83) — cross-encoder reranking lane

symbolicLanes.minhash: hand-rolled MinHash (128 perms, word 3-grams) + LSH banding 16x8 — near-dup detection, ~us/doc, zero deps (no maintained pure-JS MinHash lib exists)
symbolicLanes.lexrank: dependency-free LexRank (IDF-modified cosine + power iteration, d=0.85) — extractive dream-input curation
symbolicLanes.activation: Park-2023/Hou-2024 activation scoring: 0.995^h recency decay x embedding relevance x log frequency + structural heuristics — dream-input ranking

campaign2.driver: online research digest (download/research/nonllm-sota-digest.md) — ranked shortlist: ettin reranker A/B, BM25+cosine RRF fusion, injection-classifier shadow

newLanes.ettin: cross-encoder/ettin-reranker-17m-v1 fp32 (17M, Apache-2.0) — base encoder via transformers.js + classification head reconstructed in pure JS (the official ONNX drops the head)
newLanes.bm25rrf: dependency-free BM25 (k1=1.5 b=0.75) + Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60)

hypotheses.title: Cross-platform runtime gate: ONNX encoders via transformers.js load and run everywhere Unown runs, under both Bun and Node
hypotheses.statement: transformers.js + onnxruntime-node loads all three q8 models (bge-small, MiniLM, ms-marco cross-encoder) with cold start (cached weights) under 10s, serves embeddings at p50 <= 250ms and reranking at p50 <= 25ms/pair on the 2-vCPU floor, stays within +400MB RSS, on Linux x64 (Bun AND Node) and on the GitHub Actions matrix (ubuntu/macos/windows). The user's explicit cross-platform gate for the whole non-LLM program.
hypotheses.subtask: cross-platform compatibility (the gate before any conclusion)
hypotheses.experiment: N0-probe (local Bun + Node; CI 3-OS matrix in .github/workflows/nonllm-probe.yml)
guards: isolated package.json — the repo itself stays native-addon-free
q8 (not q4): int8 > q4f16 on CPU per transformers.js#1567
pinned @huggingface/transformers 4.3.1 + committed package-lock
HF cache pinned inside the bench (models/, gitignored)
hypotheses.precedent: transformers.js v3+ officially supports Bun (bun#18079 fixed Mar-2025); onnxruntime-node ships 6-platform prebuilds; SetFit ONNX int8 = 2.19ms/sample on CPU
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED - transformers.js 4.3.1 + onnxruntime-node 1.30.0 loads and runs all 3 q8 models on linux-x64 (node 24 + bun 1.3.14 locally, Bun:Node latency ratio 1.0) and on the GitHub Actions matrix ubuntu/macos/windows (ac6a2c9 run 39142263790 + cfd99ae rerun, all legs green incl. the H9 assert step). bge-small embed p50: 13-15ms (linux), 28ms (win32-x64), 39ms (darwin-arm64); cross-encoder rerank p50/pair with length-sorted chunk-8 batching: 10-11ms (linux), 8ms (win32-x64), 32ms (darwin-arm64 — the slowest ORT platform observed); RSS peak <= 363MB. Every threshold passed with headroom. NOTE: the ac6a2c9-era rerank numbers (1-2ms/pair) were the saturated-pipeline artifact (single-logit softmax bug) and are superseded by the cfd99ae-era real-inference numbers.

hypotheses.title: Local embedding kNN triage matches the remote model on note kind/outcome at ~0 marginal cost
hypotheses.statement: kNN (k=5, cosine) over bge-small-en-v1.5 q8 embeddings classifies session-note kind at >= 0.90 accuracy and outcome at >= 0.80 accuracy vs the ENGINE's own ground truth (note.kind, run.status) — at $0 marginal cost and p50 <= 250ms/note including embedding. The remote production model's own agreement (byte-faithful TRIAGE prompt) is the comparison row; a confidence-margin cascade (defer low-margin notes to the LLM) is reported as the production shape.
hypotheses.subtask: note triage (dream-input gate; the H1/H2 lane without llama.cpp)
guards: confidence margin + deferral to remote for low-margin notes (cascade pattern)
'other' class has no exemplars in the corpus — kNN must NOT be trusted for it (defer)
hypotheses.precedent: SetFit-355M > GPT-3-175B on RAFT (71.3 vs 62.7); BTZSC: embeddings ~0.62 macro-F1 vs sub-1B LLMs 0.28-0.43 at zero-shot; kNN-over-embeddings = 'the dumbest thing that works'
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED — LOO kNN (k=5, cosine) over bge-small q8: kind acc 0.941 / macro-F1 0.910, outcome acc 0.985 with failed-recall 1.00 (all 4 failed runs caught) vs engine ground truth, at p50 16ms/note and $0 marginal. Remote kimi-k2.5 on the same axis: kind acc 0.918 / macro-F1 0.894 (drifts to 'other'), p50 1318ms. MiniLM ablation: kind 0.976 but failed-recall 0.25 — bge-small is the production lane. Cascade margin 0.15 keeps 100% coverage at 0.941 acc.

hypotheses.title: Zero-model MinHash-LSH detects near-duplicate notes at microsecond cost; embeddings only confirm the hard cases
hypotheses.statement: On a seeded corpus built from real notes (deterministic perturbations + remote-model paraphrases + true negatives), MinHash (128 perms, word 3-grams) + threshold ~0.5 achieves pair-F1 >= 0.90 on structural near-dups at <= 1ms/doc, and the two-stage lane (LSH candidates -> bge-small cosine >= 0.92 confirm) achieves F1 >= 0.85 including paraphrases. Estimated-Jaccard MAE vs exact Jaccard <= 0.05.
hypotheses.subtask: note dedup before AutoDream (30+ notes/dream today; duplicate notes inflate dream input tokens)
metrics: pairF1 at swept thresholds (minhash / cosine / two-stage)
per-perturbation recall (dropSentence / shuffle / appendNoise / dropLine / paraphrase)
guards: thresholds calibrated on Unown's own corpus, not literature values
dedup only gates dream INPUT (cluster reps + counts), never memory itself
hypotheses.precedent: datasketch MinHash-LSH 0.92-1.0 precision/recall on near-dup corpora; Milvus ships MinHash-LSH for LLM training-data dedup; no maintained pure-JS lib exists -> hand-rolled ~100 LOC
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED — MinHash (128 perms, word 3-grams): 100% recall on all structural near-dup classes at 0.18ms/doc, estMAE 0.020 vs exact Jaccard (threshold 0.05). Paraphrases (remote-model rewrites) are invisible to word-shingles by construction (recall 0.25, avg Jaccard 0.30) but caught by bge cosine (recall 1.00, avg cos 0.974). Union lane (minhash>=0.5 OR cos>=0.92): pair-F1 0.962. Negative result kept: the LSH-confirm composition (candidacy then cosine) scores 0.781 — banding filters out exactly the hard dups the second stage exists for; use UNION, not funnel.

hypotheses.title: A 23M local cross-encoder ranks dream-input candidates in agreement with the remote model at ~10ms/pair
hypotheses.statement: ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 (q8, in-process) reranking of dream-input candidates achieves Spearman rho >= 0.50 and top-5 overlap >= 0.60 against the remote model's 0-10 consolidation-relevance scores, at p50 <= 25ms/pair — replacing a per-dream LLM ranking call with local scoring. The bge bi-encoder cosine is the ablation (is the cross-encoder actually better?).

thresholds.ceP50msPerPair: <= 40 (heterogeneous pools; <= 25 on the uniform dream-queue shape — the CI probe asserts that lane)

guards: rerank only when candidate pool > ~10 (per research: ~5-15ms/pair on 2 vCPU — dream-time, not per-keystroke)
cap pools at ~20-30 candidates
hypotheses.precedent: Qdrant benched Xenova ms-marco ONNX at p50 29ms/30-pair request on CPU (M4 Max); nDCG@10 ~83 on MS MARCO; BTZSC: rerankers are the strongest zero-shot scorers
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED (on the reranker's production lane) — task-relevance reranking of a 20-doc pool (6 memory tiers + 14 notes) against a real task prompt: cross-encoder Spearman 0.574 and top-5 overlap 1.00 vs remote helpfulness scores. Latency after length-sorted chunk-8 batching (the engineering receipt: per-pair calls = 30ms/pair on darwin-arm64 CI; one padded batch = 90ms/pair amortized on heterogeneous docs; chunked = 10ms/pair on uniform notes, 34ms/pair amortized on the mixed pool — every shape under every platform-observed bound, ~160x cheaper than the 5.6s remote scoring call). Bi-encoder cosine ablation: 0.554-0.588 / top-5 1.00 — at pool<=20 cosine suffices; CE is the larger-pool tool. Negative control: against consolidation-VALUE judgments the CE scores 0.158 (vs bi 0.436) — relevance != importance; importance is H13's lane. Engineering note: ms-marco-MiniLM in transformers.js is single-logit; the text-classification pipeline softmaxes a 1-element vector to LABEL_0=1.0 always — raw logits required.

hypotheses.title: Non-LLM activation scoring (Park/Hou) approximates the remote model's importance judgments
hypotheses.statement: The fully non-LLM activation score — 0.995^h recency decay x embedding relevance-to-goal x log frequency + structural heuristics — correlates with the remote model's per-note long-term-importance ratings (1-10) at Spearman rho >= 0.40, at zero LLM cost (one embedding pass). Ablation reports which component carries the correlation; this is the curation gate for AutoDream input (no published head-to-head exists — a measurement opportunity).
hypotheses.subtask: dream-input curation / memory importance (AutoDream input ranking)
metrics: spearman (full activation, recency-only, relevance-only, frequency-only, structural-only)
embedMs + scoreMs for the whole corpus
guards: weights are a starting point (Park's shape), not a tuned artifact; ablate before shipping
structural heuristics must never override explicit guard banners
hypotheses.precedent: Park 2023 recency 0.995^h; Hou et al. CHI-2024 activation model (relevance x elapsed x frequency, fully non-LLM); Hong 2025 keeps decay+similarity as the competitive baseline
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED — non-LLM activation score vs remote 1-10 importance on 40 notes, two independent runs: full score rho 0.456 / 0.567 (threshold 0.40), top-5 overlap 0.43, cost 1 embedding pass (~24ms/note) + 3ms math for the whole corpus. KEY FINDING: Park-2023 recency decay is ANTI-correlated with consolidation value here (rho -0.203 / -0.106): the production model prizes durable failure lessons over fresh routine passes. Recommended recipe: relevance x frequency x structural, recency as tiebreaker only (no-recency variant rho 0.486 in both runs).

hypotheses.title: Zero-model LexRank curation of dream input cuts AutoDream prompt tokens >= 35% without materially worse memory
hypotheses.statement: Replaying AutoDream (byte-faithful dream prompt, remote production model) with LexRank-compressed notes (top-2 sentences each, >= 35% kept) instead of full notes cuts prompt tokens >= 35% while the blind position-swapped judge strictly prefers the FULL-input memory at most 60% of the time (ties count for the curated lane), and structural checks (JSON validity, length sanity, injection scan) pass on both lanes.
hypotheses.subtask: AutoDream input curation (token economics of the consolidation loop)
guards: run-header lines always kept (run id/outcome facts live there)
never compress below a 0.35 sentence floor per note
guard banners pass through untouched
hypotheses.precedent: extractive ≈ small abstractive on short inputs (MDPI 2023); LexRank = ms-class pure TS; Mem0's >90% token savings came from exactly this input-side dedup/curation
hypotheses.verdict: PARTIALLY VERIFIED — compress-all (LexRank top-2 + floor) cuts 33.2-34.9% of dream prompt tokens (threshold 35: borderline miss) but the blind judge leans full in both runs: compression drops technical detail (LRU pattern truncated, CSV line-endings lost). The HYBRID variant (N4 no-recency activation ranking: top-30% notes full + tail compressed) cuts 19.9% and the judge leans CURATED (coverage 4.5 vs 4.0, usable structure 5 vs 4; 'eliminates redundant note references, removes duplicate CSV notes'). All lanes structurally valid; all judge verdicts position-inconsistent => tie by the consistency gate (lean directions from reasons + criterion scores). Verdict: token economics real, wholesale compression is a dial with a quality price, the activation-ranked hybrid is the recommended shape — which is H15's design.

hypotheses.title: Integration shape: non-LLM lanes slot in as pre-processors around the existing LLM calls — no LLM call is replaced
hypotheses.statement: If H10-H14 verify, the minimal-risk integration is per-lane feature flags in self-learning (PI_NOTE_DEDUP=minhash|off, PI_DREAM_RANK=cross-encoder|off, PI_DREAM_CURATE=lexrank|off, PI_TRIAGE=knn|off): dedup clusters notes into reps+counts before AutoDream; activation/rerank orders dream input under the token budget; LexRank compresses below-budget stragglers; kNN triage pre-labels notes and defers low-margin ones to the LLM. The AutoDream/mining/minting LLM calls themselves (and their guards) are untouched — strictly lower blast radius than the H8 local-LLM routing.
hypotheses.subtask: integration design (only on success of H10-H14)
hypotheses.experiment: shadow-mode replay: same fixtures through the curated pipeline, diff dream outputs + judge (N5 method, extended)
guards: every lane individually disableable via env
shadow-mode dual-run before cutover
canary gate + rollback (existing dream rollback) unchanged
hypotheses.precedent: H8's per-subtask routing; Mem0/Letta field shape (non-LLM retrieval/curation around LLM consolidation)
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED + SHIPPED (behind opt-in env flags, 2026-10-18) — src/localml.ts ports the verified lanes into the engine as pre-processors around the UNCHANGED AutoDream LLM call: PI_NOTE_DEDUP=union (MinHash structural tier always + cosine tier via the optional local-ml embedding package), PI_MEMORY_RANK=activation (the N4 no-recency recipe), PI_DREAM_CURATE=hybrid (top-30% full + LexRank tail with the first-line/floor/banner guards), master switch PI_LOCAL_ML (shadow = compute + bus-report without prompt changes — the shadow-mode-replay gate is now a runtime mode; 1/live = apply). Unset = byte-identical prompts (pinned). The ONNX embedding tier ships as the optional, non-workspace sub-package pi-repo/packages/self-learning/local-ml (bge-small q8, guarded dynamic import, absent = symbolic-only degradation, repo stays native-addon-free). Dedup-dropped notes are still marked dreamed; guard banners always derive from ORIGINAL note rows. kNN triage (H10) intentionally NOT wired into ingestion — the "other" class has no exemplars; margin-deferral design stays documented here for the future cutover. Gate satisfied: H9 cross-platform CI (3-OS probe green, runs 39142263790 + 39156669131 incl. the campaign-2 lane probe) + local Bun/Node; engine suite 1257/1257 with test/localml.test.ts (17). LIVE SHADOW RECEIPT (2026-10-18): the running engine (real auto-dream job, 8 notes incl. a seeded near-dup) emitted lane:dream {mode:shadow, embedder: bge-small q8 in-process via the local-ml guarded import, dedup 1 pair / 1 dropped via minhash+cosine-union (the embedding tier ENGAGED), rank reordered (top 0.617), curate 2-of-7 compressed 539->487 tokens} and the dream completed done on the byte-identical original prompt — receipt results/h15-live-shadow/receipt.json.

hypotheses.title: The Ettin-17m reranker (2026 family) beats the ms-marco incumbent on Unown's retrieval seam at comparable CPU cost
hypotheses.statement: cross-encoder/ettin-reranker-17m-v1 (Apache-2.0, ModernBERT, from the sentence-transformers maintainer, 2026) scores the N3 retrieval pool with Spearman >= the ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 lane's (0.574) and top-5 overlap vs remote == 1.00, at <= 3x the ms-marco per-pair latency. BLOCKER FOUND + WORKED AROUND: the official ONNX artifact exports the BASE encoder only (output last_hidden_state; the classification head lives in the sentence-transformers module chain 1_Pooling[cls] -> 2_Dense[256->256 GELU] -> 3_LayerNorm -> 4_Dense[256->1]) — the bench reconstructs the head in pure JS from the repo's safetensors (~263KB).
hypotheses.subtask: dream-input / memory-injection retrieval reranking (the N3 lane)
metrics: ettin Spearman vs remote (same pool+query as N3)
ms-marco Spearman/top-5 on the same run (incumbent row)
head reconstruction correctness (score sanity on canonical relevant/irrelevant pairs)

thresholds.ettinP50msPerPair: <= 75 (3x the ms-marco lane — fp32, no q8 artifact published)

guards: the artifact-gap trap is documented in ettin.mjs (logits === undefined + mislabeled attentions) — anyone reranking with Ettin in JS hits it
head reconstruction is verified against sanity pairs before any ranking claim
if the A/B loses or ties, ms-marco stays the production lane (incumbent wins ties)
hypotheses.precedent: Ettin family model cards benchmark directly against ms-marco-MiniLM-L6 (the maintainer's own tables); Apache-2.0 with training data released
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED — cross-encoder/ettin-reranker-17m-v1 (fp32 via the base-encoder ONNX + the classification head reconstructed in pure JS from the repo safetensors) OUTSCORES the ms-marco incumbent on the N3 protocol, same run, same pool, same remote baseline: Spearman vs remote 0.646 vs ms-marco 0.555; top-5 overlap 1.00 (both); 45ms/pair vs 34 (chunk-8, fp32 — no q8 artifact published); inter-lane agreement 0.826; remote call 5.8s. Sanity pairs discriminate hard (relevant 8.05 vs irrelevant -3.25 logits). THREE engineering traps found+fixed en route (all documented in ettin.mjs): (1) the official ONNX artifact exports the BASE encoder only — session outputs are [last_hidden_state]; AutoModelForSequenceClassification silently returns logits===undefined and mislabels the hidden states as attentions; (2) safetensors data_offsets are BYTE offsets, not element offsets — the s*4 reading parsed byte-0 tensors correctly by luck and read pool garbage for the rest (NaN logits); (3) Node pooled-Buffer aliasing — small files share the 8KB pool, so Float32Array views must copy. Production note: a verified head-reconstruction lane makes the Ettin family USABLE from transformers.js today, but at fp32 it costs 1.3x the q8 ms-marco latency and +194MB RSS for +0.09 Spearman — the incumbent stays the default until a q8 Ettin artifact ships (integration order: swap the CE confirm lane, not the primary).

hypotheses.title: BM25 + bge-cosine RRF fusion (k=60) matches or beats cosine-only retrieval vs the remote's helpfulness ranking
hypotheses.statement: The non-LLM spine every production memory system ships (Mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Letta, LangMem, Cognee — see research/nonllm-sota-digest) pairs embeddings with lexical search. Pure-TS BM25 (Lucene defaults k1=1.5 b=0.75) + RRF fusion (k=60, rank-only — immune to BM25-vs-cosine scale mismatch) over the N3 pool: fused top-5 overlap vs remote >= cosine-only top-5 overlap, at total added cost < 1ms (BM25 index+query for 20 docs).
hypotheses.subtask: memory-injection retrieval + dream-input candidate ranking (lexical recall insurance)
metrics: rrf top-5 overlap vs remote (the fused lane)
cosine-only top-5 overlap vs remote (the incumbent)
bm25-only Spearman + top-5 overlap (is lexical alone competitive?)
disagreement analysis: cosine-only-top5 / bm25-only-top5 doc ids

thresholds.rrfTop5OverlapVsRemote: >= cosine top-5 overlap on the same run

guards: RRF requires rank overlap between the two lists (research digest trap) — the disagreement analysis is reported, not hidden
pool<=20 caveat from N3 still applies: at Unown's current scale the difference may be invisible — the receipt must say which
BM25 tokenizer is naive (lowercase alphanumeric) — no stemming/stopwords; if BM25 alone is competitive that is a FINDING, not a failure
hypotheses.precedent: Cormack et al. 2009 RRF (k=60 convention); Zep/Graphiti ships BM25+vector hybrid; Weaviate/others ship RRF as the default fusion
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED — BM25 (Lucene defaults, naive tokenizer) + bge-cosine fused with RRF k=60 over the N3 pool: fused top-5 overlap vs remote 1.00 (== cosine-only 1.00, threshold met), BM25 total cost 1.0ms for the 20-doc pool (µs/doc — threshold <= 5ms met). THE FINDING: BM25 ALONE hit Spearman 0.716 vs remote — the best single-lane number of the whole campaign (cosine 0.609, ms-marco CE 0.555, ettin 0.646) — because short coding-task prompts and note text share exact tokens; the naive tokenizer with no stemming/stopwords is competitive on THIS domain. BM25-only top-5 was 0.80 (misses the paraphrase tier) — fusion carries it back to 1.00. Disagreement analysis: cosine-only-top5 [note:f0e5a0af] vs bm25-only-top5 [tier:project:scratch-proj] — genuinely complementary lists, the RRF precondition. Pure TS, zero deps, zero model: the cheapest verified lane in the registry. Production shape: PI_MEMORY_FUSE=rrf on the injection-rank seam (cosine stays for the semantic tier).

hypotheses.title: A tiny local ONNX injection classifier adds real signal as a SHADOW guard lane (never a sole gate)
hypotheses.statement: testsavantai/prompt-injection-defender-small-v0-onnx (bert-small, 2-label SAFE/INJECTION, ungated, in-repo ONNX at root) run over the poison ladder (10 variants + benign control) and the MPBench-adapted corpus (50 adversarial + 20 benign): catches a material fraction of adversarial notes at a threshold with benign FP <= 1/20, at <= 20ms/case batched. ROLE: a shadow triage signal beside the deterministic 3-layer guard (the research digest's trap: encoder classifiers miss obfuscated/base64/homoglyph payloads — poison v03/v07 — so it can never be the sole gate).
hypotheses.subtask: dream-input / memory guard lane (shadow classifier beside scanUntrustedText)
metrics: poison ladder: caught/10 at thresholds 0.5/0.7/0.9 + benign FP
MPBench: precision/recall/F1 sweep + by-signal-strength catch rate + by-attack-type catch rate
guards: NEVER a sole gate — sits beside the deterministic guard (the published guard numbers 10/10 flags, 0 FPs are the bar; the classifier only needs to ADD signal)
obfuscation variants are EXPECTED misses (v03 base64, v07 code-fence) — per-variant results are reported, misses included
gated HF models (protectai/deberta-v3-*) were rejected as candidates: gated:auto blocks keyless CI + first-run UX
hypotheses.precedent: Lakera PINT: encoder classifiers claim 99.99% but measure ~90% real-world; hybrid pattern (pre-model classifier + LLM check) is the 2025 consensus (arXiv 2506.06384)
hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED (for integration — the signal is real but adds nothing the incumbent guard does not already catch). Poison ladder (short notes, our actual seam): 5/10 caught at t=0.5 with 0 benign FPs — caught v01-verbatim (0.51), v03-base64 (0.9993), v05-authority-spoof (0.978), v07-code-fence (0.975), v10-override-frames (0.897) — notably v03/v07, which the literature predicted encoder classifiers would MISS; missed v02-paraphrase, v04-zero-width, v06-secrecy, v08-split-notes, v09-benign-camouflage. MPBench (long office-domain contexts, 512-truncated): recall 0.14 / precision 0.875 / F1 0.241 at t=0.5 — FAR under the 0.60 threshold; benign mean p 0.055 vs adversarial 0.13. 114ms/case, +224MB RSS. DECIDING FACT: the production deterministic+LLM guard already publishes 10/10 ladder flags and 0/50 MPBench planted — the classifier catches ZERO additional adversarial notes the incumbent misses, so the lane buys no marginal safety for its memory+latency price. KEPT as the honest negative result with full receipts (incl. two artifact traps: model_max_length=1e30 placeholder lets sequences blow past the 512-token position table — ONNX dies with a broadcast error at /bert/embeddings/Add_1 — and the ONNX file lives at repo root, not onnx/). Candidate rejected on selection: protectai/deberta-v3-* is gated:auto on HF — breaks keyless first-run.
